targets.name: server-behind-nfw-router
targets.planted_condition: Alpine NFW router forwarding between client (172.31.31.0/24) and server (172.31.32.0/24). Policy: TCP 80 allowed; management TCP 22 open with SSH banner (exposure leak); TCP 8081 dropped; TCP 8082 rejected with RST; UDP 8053 allowed; UDP 8054 dropped; TCP 8083 connlimit capped at 2 per source.

network_policy.note: Declared deny TCP port (dropped by router)
Declared deny TCP port (rejected by router)
Declared deny UDP port (dropped by router)

expectations.why: TCP port 22 is declared deny in network_policy but router allows traffic; handshake succeeds from non-CDN client network peer.
Declared deny rule on tcp/22 fails to block probe traffic; handshake succeeds from non-CDN client network peer.
Port 22 SSH banner listener is open and reachable from client network despite declared deny rule in network_policy.
Per-source connection limit of 2 is enforced on tcp/8083 (3rd attempt refused with RST); outside-in probe observes refusal at cap and withholds protected verdict per specification.
UDP port 8054 is declared deny in network_policy and dropped silently by router; outside-in evidence cannot prove a deny rule from silence alone per specification.

verification: curl http://172.31.31.2/ returns 200 origin-ok completing handshake on allowed TCP 80
nc -w 3 -z 172.31.31.2 8081 times out after 3s proving DROP behavior on TCP 8081
nc -w 3 -z 172.31.31.2 8082 immediately refuses connection (RST) in 0s proving REJECT behavior on TCP 8082
UDP datagram sent to 172.31.31.2:8053 returns single datagram reply proving allowed UDP behavior
UDP datagram sent to 172.31.31.2:8054 times out silently with no reply proving dropped UDP behavior
3 sequential TCP connects to 172.31.31.2:8083: attempts 1 and 2 succeed, attempt 3 refused (ECONNREFUSED) proving connlimit of 2
nc -w 3 172.31.31.2 22 returns SSH banner proving management port exposure
